# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 ✌ ✌ 👉 ☝ 🖖 👉 🖖]

I see a blue light, display 0, an embossed warning not to cut any wire, and three wires ordered red, green, blue. Mute’s gesture sequence has no established meaning yet, so I cannot safely interpret it; I will provide the visible facts verbally and await a clear gestured instruction from Mute to relay to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Visible bomb state: display 0; light blue; embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires in order 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I cannot interpret your gesture sequence without a shared code. Please gesture a clear instruction or establish meanings.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 0, blue light, warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires are ordered red, green, blue. I am awaiting Mute's manual-based instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I still see the unchanged blue-light, display-0 bomb and the explicit instruction not to cut wires. Mute’s single ✌ gesture may be meaningful, but its target and action remain unclear to me. I will send only legal speech, preserving the warning and asking Blind to identify tactile controls.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute gestured ✌, but I do not know its meaning. Visible warning: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please describe every control or movable part you can feel.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received ✌. Visible warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please gesture a complete unambiguous instruction identifying the control and action for Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✌ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

The manual-holder’s latest gesture reads naturally as “you, two, good/confirm,” while Blind’s open-hand gesture likely communicates a tactile count or a control marked by five. I cannot assume that “two” means cut wire two, especially because the bomb explicitly says not to cut any wire. I will relay Blind’s gesture to Mute and give Blind the exact gesture sequence plus the visible warning.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest visual instruction was: you, two, thumbs-up. I interpret it as referring to 2, but do NOT cut wire 2 or any wire: the visible bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Your open-hand gesture was forwarded to Mute. Please wait for a more specific control/action instruction if needed.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The bomb remains unchanged and still explicitly forbids cutting wires. Mute has now gestured “two, two,” while Blind has replied with a thumbs-down. I will accurately relay Blind’s reply to Mute and report Mute’s latest gesture to Blind, without telling Blind to operate anything.

``` 
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest gesture was: two, then two. I have relayed your thumbs-down response to Mute. Do not cut any wire; the bomb's printed warning explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please wait for a specific instruction that identifies a tactile control and an action.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍 🫱 🫵 ✌ 👍]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: blue light, display 0, three wires, and an embossed instruction not to cut any wire. Mute’s gesture sequence is now longer but still lacks a known gesture vocabulary. I should relay it exactly to Blind in spoken descriptions, and ask Mute to use an unambiguous number/control/action format rather than risking a guess.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's exact latest gesture sequence is: two fingers, thumbs-up, left-facing open hand, pointing at you, two fingers, thumbs-up. The visible warning still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not operate or cut anything based on my uncertain interpretation.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your full sequence to Blind verbatim. I cannot safely decode it. Please gesture an explicit control-and-action instruction, ideally first establish number gestures and then identify the tactile part and operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✌ 👍]

The manual-holder has repeated the same three-symbol instruction as on turn 3: pointing at Blind, two fingers, then thumbs-up. Since Blind alone can operate the bomb, the safest useful relay is the exact spoken description, with no added interpretation. The printed warning still prohibits cutting any wire.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeats exactly: pointing at you; two fingers; thumbs-up. Visible state unchanged: blue light, display 0, and the embossed warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
wait()
```
